RADICAL HOPE FROM GAZA: A COLLECTION OF ESSAYS BY AYA AL-HATTAB

An Introduction from the Editors-in-Chief of Solarpunk Magazine

What does it mean to hold on to hope when the world around you is being destroyed? What does it mean to imagine a better future when even the possibility of an ordinary tomorrow feels uncertain at best?

In this powerful six-part series, Palestinian writer and journalist Aya Al-Hattab takes us into the lived realities of Gaza, offering an intimate and deeply human perspective on war, occupation, displacement, loss, and the struggle to preserve hope. Through personal reflections, historical examination, and stories of everyday compassion, Al-Hattab reveals the profound consequences of violence on people, communities, animals, and the places they call home.

Throughout these essays, a central truth emerges: hope requires the courage to imagine a future beyond the suffering of the present, even when that future feels impossibly distant. Sometimes that hope takes the form of caring for a beloved animal, remembering a familiar street, or simply dreaming of a home filled with books and loved ones.

title: Solarpunk Horror, Lunarpunk Submissions, and 2027 Magazine Submissions
content:
We’ve got some exciting announcements to share! There’s a brand-new lunarpunk anthology seeking submissions, our special horror-themed issue of Solarpunk Magazine is available for preorder, we’re going to start publishing solarpunk novellas and novels, and our complete 2027 submissions schedule is now up on our website’s submissions page.

So whether you’re a reader looking for your next great story or a writer dreaming up better futures, here’s what’s coming.

Submission Window: November 1 – December 31, 2026

Android Press is preparing to venture into the shadows with What Blooms in Darkness: A Lunarpunk Anthology, edited by our co-editor-in-chief, Justine Norton-Kertson, and scheduled for publication in autumn 2027.

Lunarpunk shares solarpunk’s commitment to ecological regeneration, social justice, community, and liberatory futures, while exploring the possibilities that emerge in darkness, mystery, privacy, dreams, and the hidden corners of our world.

What Blooms in Darkness asks some fascinating questions: What kinds of communities thrive beyond the reach of surveillance? What knowledge survives underground? What forms of liberation become possible when people are free to remain unseen?

Android Press is seeking stories about everything from nocturnal ecosystems and underground communities to secret mutual-aid networks, hidden cultures, rituals, and resistance movements.
